scope: B2C E-Commerce Platform/backend/services/order — state machine, ownership, internal-auth, outbox/consumer, list/detail handlers, migrations 001-006

verified_ok: Sole-writer rule: only orders/access/storage_order.go:121 UpdateStatus writes orders.status. grep across backend/services/* shows no other UPDATE on "order".orders. (Identity/Catalog/Payment/Checkout UPDATE *their own* tables only.)

payment.completed consumer (consumer.go:51-133) does SELECT ... FOR UPDATE via GetByIDForUpdate, status!=PENDING_PAYMENT branch logs and commits without mutation; only PENDING_PAYMENT path performs UPDATE+history insert in same tx.
Two-layer dedup: consumed_events INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (event_id) DO NOTHING present in storage_consumed_event.go:33-47 and called inside tx before the FOR UPDATE.
order_items immutable: StorageOrderItem interface (service.go:25) exposes no Update; access/storage_order_item.go has no UPDATE statement. grep '"UPDATE order_items"' returns zero hits.
Order.detail customer path returns 404 (CodeOrderNotOwned) for both not-found and not-yours — no existence leak (handler_detail.go:71-77).

Pagination bounds enforced server-side: defaultListLimit=20, maxListLimit=100, page<1 normalised to 1 (handler_list_mine.go:48-58). Negative offset impossible since offset = (page-1)*limit and page>=1.
ValidateTransition is pure: state_machine.go has no DB/IO imports; only fmt.
Internal secret sourced from env INTERNAL_SHARED_SECRET via env:"...,notEmpty" (config/config.go:69); never logged (no slog references to SharedSecret).

Order number date prefix derived in Go from now.UTC().Format("20060102") and passed to NextOrderNumber, which uses nextval() inside the SAME tx as INSERT (handler_create_from_checkout.go:41-66, storage_order.go:29-36) — ORD-008 single global sequence, gaps acceptable, no cross-day mismatch within a single request.

findings.title: Internal-auth shared-secret compared with non-constant-time `!=`
findings.evidence: middleware_internal_auth.go:34 — `if supplied == "" || supplied != sharedSecret`. Go string `!=` short-circuits at the first differing byte and is timing-observable across a network. Internal endpoints (create-from-checkout, cancel-on-checkout-failure) are the ONLY way to mint orders or compensate-cancel; secret recovery = full bypass of the trust boundary between Checkout and Order.
findings.fix: Use `crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare([]byte(supplied), []byte(sharedSecret)) == 1` and length-check via the same primitive, OR migrate to mTLS / SERVICE-role JWT (already noted as deferred in AMBIG-ORD-1).
findings.residual: Even with constant-time compare, a long-lived shared secret in env is a weak control; mTLS remains the target.

findings.title: payment.completed consumer does NOT emit any outbox event — acceptable here, but onPaymentFailed/Expired/onReservationExpired are stubs that will need outbox emission for downstream parity
findings.evidence: consumer.go:135-156 — three handlers are TODO stubs. Spec says events.order.cancelled outbox row must be written in same tx as the orders UPDATE + status_history INSERT for CANCELLED transitions. Currently NO handler in the codebase emits to outbox; only handler_cancel_mine and handler_cancel_on_checkout_failure are stubbed (501) and handler_update_status_admin is stubbed.
findings.fix: Before MVP go-live, implement the three stub consumers and the three cancel/admin handlers with the documented in-tx pattern: UPDATE + history INSERT + (for cancellation) outbox INSERT. State machine and storage already support it.
findings.residual: Cart/Inventory cannot react to cancellations until cancel paths land. Track as feature-gap, not a new vulnerability.

findings.title: create-from-checkout logs userId at INFO; buyer_email and address are not logged (good), but slog default JSON handler may capture full request via auto-logging middleware
findings.evidence: handler_create_from_checkout.go:169-173 logs orderId/orderNumber/userId — no email/address. Confirmed grep on buyer_email/address_snapshot inside log calls = zero. However router.go:41 wires `middleware.AutoLoggingMiddleware` (common/middleware) — body-logging behaviour not in this scope; PII risk depends on that middleware's redaction policy.
findings.fix: Confirm common/middleware.AutoLoggingMiddleware redacts request body or excludes the create-from-checkout route; otherwise add a body-redact rule for buyerEmail and addressSnapshot.
findings.residual: Out-of-scope for L1 order review; flag for cross-cutting reviewer.

findings.title: Admin role check in detail handler reads `claims.Extra["role"]` as string with default CUSTOMER — ok, but no defense-in-depth role check on /list-admin, /update-status-admin (currently stubs)
findings.evidence: handler_detail.go:161-169 (claimRole) defaults to CUSTOMER on missing/typed-wrong claim — safe-by-default. handler_list_admin.go and handler_update_status_admin.go are 501 stubs; when implemented they MUST call claimRole(claims)=="ADMIN" and return 403 AUTH_FORBIDDEN before any DB access.
findings.fix: Extract a `requireAdmin(c) error` helper and call from every admin handler entry; pair with route-level middleware that enforces role==ADMIN at the adminGroup in router.go.
findings.residual: Stub-only today; risk = future regression if implemented without the helper.

open_questions: Does common/middleware.AutoLoggingMiddleware log request bodies in PRD? (Affects PII finding ORD-REV-L1-003.)
Is the route-level adminGroup expected to gain a RequireAdmin middleware, or is per-handler check the convention? (TD/ARCH should clarify.)
